payload.claim: `_seed_unreadable`'s docstring claims 'Seven paths `file_at` cannot read as text, plus `src/gone_link.py`'s own target,' but the function writes exactly seven paths total (vendor/sub, src/out.py, src/hop.py, src/c_link.py, src/gone.py, src/gone_link.py, src/latin.py), and the test itself proves `src/c_link.py` is readable (it returns successfully, grouped with `src/c.py`, in the final assertions). So only six of the seven are unreadable as text, and `src/gone.py` ('gone_link.py's own target') is already one of those seven, not an additional eighth path. The docstring overcounts by double-booking `gone.py` as a 'plus' item while also miscounting how many of the seven are actually unreadable.
